segments.t: This tab lets you choose your own shortcuts for korTTY's commands: give a menu command other keys, give a command without a shortcut one, or remove a shortcut you keep pressing by accident. Open via KTPH001Configuration → Global Settings → KeyboardKTPH002; stored in KTPH000.
a key with KTPH005KTPH000KTPH006, KTPH007KTPH001KTPH008 or KTPH009KTPH002KTPH010, KTPH011KTPH003KTPH012 to KTPH013KTPH004KTPH014 on their own, or none

The list holds every command of the window's menu bar, also the ones without a shortcut, in menu order. Its columns are the KTPH003ActionKTPH004, the KTPH005MenuKTPH006 it is in (its menu path, as the KTPH007command paletteKTPH008 shows it), the KTPH009ShortcutKTPH010 and a KTPH011StatusKTPH012: empty for a command on its default shortcut, KTPH013ChangedKTPH014 or KTPH015RemovedKTPH016 for one you changed, KTPH017FixedKTPH018 for a shortcut that cannot be changed, KTPH019Also used by …KTPH020 for a KTPH021conflictKTPH022 and KTPH023Not used hereKTPH024 for a stored shortcut this computer KTPH025does not acceptKTPH026. Type part of a command's name, its menu or its keys into KTPH027Filter by action, menu or shortcutKTPH028 to find it, for example KTPH000, KTPH001 or KTPH002, and tick KTPH029Only changedKTPH030 to list only the commands you changed.
Select the command in the list.

Click the shortcut field below the list and press the new combination. Holding a modifier on its own records nothing, so press KTPH004KTPH000KTPH005, KTPH006KTPH001KTPH007, KTPH008KTPH002KTPH009 or KTPH010KTPH003KTPH011 together with the key.

The field takes the key press as the command's new shortcut and the list shows it as KTPH002ChangedKTPH003; a combination korTTY cannot use is KTPH004refusedKTPH005 with the reason below the field, and the command keeps its shortcut. While the field records, KTPH006KTPH000KTPH007 ends recording without a change and KTPH008KTPH001KTPH009 leaves the field. KTPH010Remove ShortcutKTPH011 leaves the command without a key, KTPH012Reset to DefaultKTPH013 gives it its own shortcut back, and KTPH014Reset AllKTPH015 puts every command back on its default. Pressing the default shortcut in the field is the same as KTPH016Reset to DefaultKTPH017. The line below the field shows the default shortcut of the selected command.

Saving applies the shortcuts at once in every open window, without a restart: the menus show the new keys, and so does the command palette. A shortcut you choose also works while a terminal has the focus: korTTY runs the command instead of passing the keys to the shell, and whatever character they would type is kept out of the terminal, so it never reaches the shell or, in broadcast mode, the other panes. A function key you give a command therefore no longer reaches the programs in the terminal, such as KTPH000 or KTPH001.
korTTY does not take a key away from the shell or the system, so these combinations are refused when you record them:

A shortcut that another command already uses is taken, so you can swap the shortcuts of two commands in two steps. Until each shortcut is used by one command only, both rows show KTPH000Also used by …KTPH001 in red, a line above the list names the shared shortcuts, and the KTPH002KeyboardKTPH003 tab shows a red number. KTPH004SaveKTPH005 then keeps the dialog open and shows the Keyboard tab with the first conflict selected: change or remove one shortcut of each pair to save.
Shortcuts from another computer or versionKTPH000

A shortcut is stored for every platform at once: one you record with KTPH006KTPH000KTPH007 on a Mac is the same shortcut with KTPH008KTPH001KTPH009 on Windows and Linux. When a settings file holds a shortcut that this computer refuses, such as KTPH010KTPH002KTPH011+KTPH012KTPH003KTPH013 from a Mac, which is KTPH014KTPH004KTPH015+KTPH016KTPH005KTPH017 and belongs to the shell on Linux, the command's row shows KTPH018Not used hereKTPH019 and the reason, the command keeps its default shortcut here, and the stored shortcut stays in the file for the Mac. Shortcuts of commands that this version of korTTY does not have, from a newer version, are kept as well, and a note above the list names them. A settings file from a version without this tab opens with every default.

In KTPH000 each changed command is one entry such as KTPH001, or KTPH002 for a removed shortcut, inside KTPH003. The name before KTPH004 is the command's id; KTPH005 means KTPH009KTPH007KTPH010 on macOS and KTPH011KTPH008KTPH012 on Windows and Linux, while KTPH006 is the Control key itself on every platform. An entry korTTY cannot read is ignored.
